response.answer: The Monument to the Discoveries in Lisbon is open from 10:00 to 18:00 (admission ends at 5:30 PM) daily, except on 1 January, 1 May, 24, 25, and 31 December. The admission price is €10 for adults, €5 for youth aged 13–25, €8.50 for those over 65, and €7 for visitors with specific needs. The outside, the prow, and the compass rose are free at any hour. The National Museum of Ancient Art in Lisbon's opening hours and ticket prices are not provided in the sources.

results.content:
## Key facts

### Opening hours

|  |  |
 --- |
| Daily, March–September | 10:00–19:00 |
| Daily, October–February | 10:00–18:00 |

Closed 1 January, 1 May, 24, 25 and 31 December; last entry 30 minutes before closing

### Admission

Adult
:   €10 (about $12)

Reduced
:   €5 (about $6) youth 13–25; €8.50 (about $10) 65 and over; €7 (about $8) visitors with specific needs [...] The outside, the prow and the compass rose are free at any hour. Going inside for the lift to the viewpoint, the exhibition and the film costs €10 (about $12), €5 for 13–25s and €8.50 for over-65s, free under 12 and free with the Lisboa Card. Lisbon residents enter free on Sunday mornings; visitors do not.

  

### Is the Monument to the Discoveries worth it? [...] Quick answer Free outside, €10 inside, open on Mondays — and who the figures are 

The Monument to the Discoveries is free to walk around and costs €10 (about $12) to go inside, where a lift takes you to the viewpoint 50-odd metres up and the ticket also covers the exhibition and a film. It is open every day, 10:00–19:00 from March to September and 10:00–18:00 from October to February, with last entry half an hour before closing.

Key takeaways
